{
"Object-Oriented Design": "A software design paradigm that organizes systems around objects—entities combining data and behavior—using principles such as encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism to model real-world concepts.",
"Inheritance": "A mechanism in object-oriented design by which one class derives properties and behaviors from another, enabling code reuse and the modeling of hierarchical relationships between types.",
"Hierarchy": "A structured arrangement of classes or types in which more specialized entities are organized under more general ones, often formed through inheritance relationships.",
"Composition": "A design technique in which complex objects are built by combining simpler objects as components, favoring flexible assembly over rigid inheritance-based reuse.",
"Encapsulation": "The principle of bundling data and behavior within an object while hiding its internal state and implementation details behind a well-defined interface.",
"Implementation Detail": "An internal aspect of a component's realization—such as data structures or algorithms—that is hidden from external consumers and may change without affecting the interface.",
"Polymorphism": "The ability for objects of different types to be treated through a common interface, allowing uniform operations whose behavior varies according to the actual object type.",
"Object": "A runtime instance in object-oriented programming that encapsulates state and behavior according to the definition of its class or type.",
"Type": "A classification that specifies the structure, behavior, and allowable operations of values or objects, enabling type-based reasoning and polymorphism.",
"Interface": "A declaration of a set of operations and their signatures that a class or object must provide, defining a contract without prescribing how it is implemented.",
"Contract": "A formal agreement specifying the expected behavior, inputs, outputs, and guarantees between a provider (such as an interface) and its consumers.",
"Liskov Substitution Principle": "A principle of object-oriented design stating that objects of a derived class must be usable wherever instances of its base class are expected, without altering program correctness.",
"Derived Class": "A class that inherits from another class (the base class), extending or specializing its behavior and data while conforming to its contract.",
"Base Class": "A class from which other classes inherit, providing common attributes, methods, and interface contracts that derived classes extend or override.",
"Class": "A blueprint or template in object-oriented programming that defines the structure, behavior, and interface of its instances (objects)."
}
